title: The three together (3.4–3.8)
hook: concentration, meditation and absorption on one object get a single name, samyama, the tool the rest of book three is built on

segments.voice: Yesterday: concentration, meditation, absorption. Hold the mind, let it flow, and disappear into it.

Watch someone braid hair. Three strands, each one loose and floppy on its own. Left over middle. Right over middle. Again, again. Somewhere along the way, three strands stop being three strands. They become one braid, strong enough to hold its shape all day. Nobody would call it three things anymore. Patanjali braids the three inner limbs, and the braid gets its own name, a name that will carry the rest of book three.

Sutra 3.4: the three together are samyama. Sam means together. Yama you already know, from the first limb: reining in, holding. Samyama, holding together. Concentration, meditation and absorption, all on the same object, at once. From here on, whenever Patanjali says, by samyama on this, that happens, this is the tool he means. Sutra 3.5: by mastering it, the light of insight. Prajna, wisdom, begins to shine. Sutra 3.6: it's applied in stages. You don't jump to the top. The classical commentary adds a striking line here: yoga is to be known by yoga, and yoga grows out of yoga. Each stage, practiced, opens the next. Then inside and outside. Sutra 3.7: these three are inner, compared with the five limbs before: the restraints, the observances, the seat, the breath, the senses drawing back. And then 3.8, the humbling line: even these are outer, compared with the seedless. Remember seedless samadhi, from the end of book one? Absorption with no object at all, no seed left to sprout. Measured against that, even the braid is still on the outside. So samyama is powerful, and Patanjali is about to spend most of a book on what it can do. But he's said up front: it isn't the end of the road.
screen: `SAMYAMA: HOLDING TOGETHER.` · `MASTERED, INSIGHT SHINES.` · `YOGA IS KNOWN BY YOGA.` · `EVEN THESE ARE OUTER TO THE SEEDLESS.` · then, large: `SAMYAMA.`

segments.voice: Choose one object, the breath at the nose or a single sound, hold the mind there, and let the holding become a flow. If for a moment there's only the breath and no one doing the breathing, let that be. Often the mind stays on the first strand, and that's the work.
Prajna, wisdom's light, which begins to shine when samyama is mastered: concentration, meditation and absorption held on one object at once, the tool of book three.
Your line: samyama. Three strands, one object, one braid that holds. That's day four sixty-six.

howItsDone: Teachers of the Yoga Sutras present samyama as the combined practice of the three inner limbs on a single object, learned gradually over years, and they stress that its insights are steps toward liberation rather than the goal.

fork.setup: you've read every book on samyama and want to skip straight to the highest stage. what does sutra 3.6 say?
options: start at the highest and work down.
fork.reveal: 3.6: its application is in stages. the commentary adds that yoga is known by yoga: the next stage teaches itself.

original.note: Sanskrit saṃyama: sam (together) plus yama (holding, restraint); dhāraṇā, dhyāna and samādhi on one object.

trapdoor: what you thought: samyama is self-control.
what it means: concentration, meditation and absorption braided on one object, the tool book three uses for everything that follows.
what a scholar hears: 3.4 defines it; 3.5 prajna-aloka; 3.7 antar-anga; 3.8 calls even these bahir-anga, outer, to nirbija samadhi.
guess: wisdom's light, shining when samyama is mastered

chat.says: If samyama is so powerful, is it the final goal of yoga?
options: No, Patanjali says samyama is still outer next to seedless samadhi, with no seed left.
Yes, once those three steps are woven together, yoga's whole work is done.
Yes, samyama is the seedless samadhi itself, just under another name.
chat.meaning: Sutra 3.8 says the three inner limbs are still outer compared with the seedless: absorption with no object and no seed left to sprout.
